name: Civic Almanac
description: An open, versioned index of public civic and government data.

entries.title: Census Bureau Voting and Registration (CPS November Supplement)
entries.description: The Census Bureau's estimates of voter registration and turnout among U.S. citizens by age, sex, race, education, and other characteristics, from the Current Population Survey's November supplement in every national election since 1964.
entries.attribution: U.S. Census Bureau, Current Population Survey, Voting and Registration Supplement
entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page says "For every national election since 1964, we collected data on the characteristics of American voters". The tables page lists "Voting and Registration in the Election of November 2024" (April 2025). It notes "The P20 detailed tables are released every two years following national level elections" and that tables come in XLS, CSV, and PDF. Releases follow the two-year election cycle; the schema has no biennial value, so cadence is irregular.

entries.title: Congress.gov API
entries.description: The Library of Congress's public API for U.S. legislative data from Congress.gov — bills, amendments, actions, members, committees, congressional records, and more.

coverage.temporal: multiple Congresses (coverage varies by data type)

entries.notes: Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 for api.congress.gov. It says "Congress.gov shares its application programming interface (API) with the public" and asks users to "Sign up for an API key from api.data.gov". It documents /v3 endpoints such as GET /bill. The www.congress.gov web site returned 403 (bot protection) to curl this session; civic-almanac runs the headless checker. Two things come from the API's usual documentation and weren't checked: the daily update cadence and the xml format option.

entries.title: EAC Election Administration & Voting Survey (EAVS)
entries.description: The U.S. Election Assistance Commission's biennial survey of how elections are administered nationwide — registration, turnout, mail ballots, polling places, and election technology.
entries.notes: Conducted after each federal general election (biennial).

entries.title: European Parliament Election Results 2024
entries.description: The European Parliament's official results site for the 2024 European elections: results by country and political group, seat distribution, and turnout, with the constitutive session composition.

coverage.temporal: 2024 European elections (with historical results back to 1979 on the site)

entries.license: EP legal notice — reuse authorised, including commercial, with the source acknowledged; not a Creative Commons licence (see notes)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (redirects to /en/). The disclaimer reads "The final update to data on this website took place on 6 September 2024", which is a publisher declaration that the data is static, so status is frozen. For the current composition of political groups, the site points to the MEPs section of the EP website. The historical results back to 1979 and the download formats weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: the site's legal notice (https://elections.europa.eu/en/legal-notice/) says reuse of EU-owned textual data and multimedia "is authorised, for personal use or for further non-commercial or commercial dissemination, provided that the entire item is reproduced and the source is acknowledged", adds that "the reuse of certain data may be subject to different conditions in some instances", and asks that a partial reproduction cite the URL. It is a site-wide notice; the download-datasheets page (json/csv) states no licence of its own.

entries.title: House Oversight Committee Release of Epstein Records Provided by the Department of Justice (2 September 2025)
entries.description: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform's release of 33,295 pages of Epstein-related records produced to it by the U.S. Department of Justice under a committee subpoena of 5 August 2025. DOJ's own Epstein Library links to this release as its "House Disclosures".
entries.publisher: U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

access.auth_note: Files are hosted on Google Drive, with a Dropbox backup, both linked from the committee's release page.

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

entries.license: unverified — DOJ-produced records (mixed; DOJ-authored portions are US Gov works, third-party and court material is not); no reuse terms stated on the release page
entries.attribution: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, Epstein records provided by the Department of Justice
entries.notes:
VERTICAL: congressional release; this probably belongs in civic-almanac. It is cross-linked from DOJ's Epstein Library, so justice-almanac may want a pointer.
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (plain curl with a browser User-Agent). The page "Oversight Committee Releases Epstein Records Provided by the Department of Justice" is "Published: Sep 2, 2025". It says the committee "released 33,295 pages of Epstein-related records that were provided by the U.S. Department of Justice. On August 5, Chairman Comer issued a subpoena for records related to Mr. Jeffrey Epstein". It links "Epstein-related documents can be found here" (Google Drive) and "Backup access can be found here" (Dropbox).
Authority: committee subpoena of 5 Aug 2025. Redaction, as stated on the page: "the Department of Justice has indicated it will continue producing those records while ensuring the redaction of victim identities and any child sexual abuse material", so redaction was done by DOJ before production. No "last updated" date is shown.
Hosting caveat: the files sit in third-party consumer storage linked from the .gov page, so the link checker should watch the Drive and Dropbox links as well.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no licence on the page, and https://oversight.house.gov/copyright/ returns 404. Folder contents, formats and file counts were not checked, and the Drive and Dropbox folders were not opened.

entries.title: House Oversight Committee Releases of Records Provided by the Epstein Estate (2025)
entries.description: The House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform's public releases of records produced to it by the estate of Jeffrey Epstein under a committee subpoena of 25 August 2025. Releases were made on 8 September 2025 and 12 November 2025, the latter "an additional 20,000 pages".
entries.publisher: U.S. House of Representatives, Committee on Oversight and Government Reform

access.auth_note: Files are hosted on Google Drive, with a Dropbox backup, both linked from the committee's release pages.

recovery.notes: Wayback capture made while the resource was live.

entries.license: unverified — records produced to the Committee by the Epstein estate are not US Gov works; no reuse terms stated on the release pages
entries.attribution: U.S. House Committee on Oversight and Government Reform, records provided by the Epstein Estate
entries.notes:
VERTICAL: congressional release; this probably belongs in civic-almanac rather than justice-almanac.
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200 (plain curl with a browser User-Agent). The canonical page is "Oversight Committee Releases Records Provided by the Epstein Estate, Chairman Comer Provides Statement" ("Published: Sep 8, 2025"). It says the committee "released records provided by the estate of Jeffrey Epstein pursuant to Chairman James Comer's (R-Ky.) subpoena issued on August 25, 2025". It links the subpoena (https://oversight.house.gov/wp-content/uploads/2025/08/2025.08.25-Subpoena-and-Schedule-to-Epstein-Estate.pdf, HTTP 200), and says "The documents can be found here (backup here)": a Google Drive folder and a Dropbox folder.
Second release: "Oversight Committee Releases Additional Epstein Estate Documents" ("Published: Nov 12, 2025"; https://oversight.house.gov/release/oversight-committee-releases-additional-epstein-estate-documents/, HTTP 200). It says the committee "released an additional 20,000 pages of documents received from the estate", again with Google Drive and Dropbox links.
Hosting caveat: the committee's .gov pages are canonical, but the files sit in third-party consumer storage that the committee controls through links only. Those links are more fragile than the .gov page, so the link checker should also watch them. Search results mention a further estate set around 16 Sep 2025 and committee figures of "approximately 65,000 pages" across all releases. Neither was verified on a committee release page.
Authority: committee subpoena (25 Aug 2025). Redaction: neither release page states a redaction policy. The 8 Sep page says the committee withheld bank-account information ("The Committee will pursue these bank records"). No "last updated" date is shown.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: no licence or reuse terms on the release pages, and https://oversight.house.gov/copyright/ returns 404. The committee's press text is a federal government work; the estate's documents are not. Formats, page counts per folder and file contents were not checked, and the Drive and Dropbox folders were not opened.

entries.title: International IDEA Voter Turnout Database
entries.description: The most comprehensive global collection of voter turnout statistics for presidential and parliamentary elections since 1945, plus European Parliament elections, using both registered voters and voting-age population as bases.
entries.publisher: International Institute for Democracy and Electoral Assistance (International IDEA)

access.auth_note: Export may require accepting International IDEA's release agreement.

entries.license: IDEA terms and conditions — copyright reserved; non-commercial use only; no Creative Commons licence stated for the database (see notes)
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-10-31: HTTP 200. The page calls it "the most comprehensive global collection of voter turnout statistics from presidential and parliamentary elections since 1945", including European Parliament elections, with an "Export data" option. The footer reads "© 2026 International IDEA. All Rights Reserved", so this is not open-licensed. It is cataloged for authority; reusers should read IDEA's terms. Jurisdiction is multilateral because International IDEA is an intergovernmental organization of member states. The export formats weren't checked.
Licence checked 2026-10-31: IDEA's terms (https://www.idea.int/terms-and-conditions) say users of its Data, Tools and Publications "are not permitted to benefit commercially from their use", and that Data or Tools may carry their own licence terms shown on access; none are shown on the database or export pages. Creative Commons covers only some PDF publications (the 2018 codebook is CC BY-NC-SA 3.0, which licenses the document, not the data). The footer's "Release Agreement Form" is a consent form for event speakers and contributors, not a data agreement.

entries.description: Online catalog of the holdings of the U.S. National Archives (NARA) — archival descriptions, authority records, digitized records, and public contributions, with a read/write API.
entries.publisher: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration (NARA)

entries.title: UK Electoral Commission Research, Reports and Data
entries.description: The Electoral Commission's data and reports on UK elections and referendums: electorate size, turnout and rejected ballots collected after each poll, electoral registration research, electoral fraud data, and public attitudes surveys.

coverage.spatial: United Kingdom (England, Scotland, Wales, Northern Ireland)
coverage.temporal: varies by election (2026 Scottish Parliament, Senedd and English local election reports seen)

entries.license: unverified — no copyright or reuse terms page could be read on electoralcommission.org.uk (Cloudflare challenge; /copyright returned 404)
entries.attribution: Electoral Commission, Research, reports and data
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01 in headless Chromium: HTTP 200 once the Cloudflare check passed (curl and a first Chromium load got 403 "Just a moment..."; later loads in the same check were intermittent). The page says "Following elections and referendums, we collect data such as the size of the electorate, turnout and rejected ballot papers" and lists "Report on the 2026 England mayoral and local government elections", "Report on the 2026 Scottish Parliament election" and "Report on the 2026 Senedd elections", plus sections "Election and referendum data and reports", "Electoral registration research" and "Electoral fraud data". The election data sub-page stayed behind Cloudflare for me, so I did not see the data files or their formats. Party finance is cataloged separately as uk-electoral-commission-political-finance.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: not verified. The footer shows only "© 2026 Electoral Commission"; /copyright returned 404 and /site-map "Access denied", and no terms page is linked from the footer (Contact, Media centre, About us, FOI, Accessibility, Privacy policy, Publication scheme, Procurement). Open Knowledge's 2014-15 Open Data Index pages say the Commission moved its election data to the Open Government Licence in October 2013, but that is secondary and old, so no licence is asserted.

entries.title: UK Electoral Commission Political Finance Database
entries.description: The Electoral Commission's searchable registers of UK political parties, non-party campaigners and referendum participants, with its database of reported donations, loans, election and referendum spending, and party accounts, downloadable as CSV.

coverage.temporal: varies by register (Q2 2026 donations and October 2026 regulated donee donations latest seen)

entries.license: unverified — the search site and electoralcommission.org.uk show no reuse terms that could be read
entries.notes:
Human-verified 2026-11-01: HTTP 200 (curl and headless Chromium); the root redirects to a default donations search. The page says "This page allows you to search the registers of Political Parties, Non-party campaigners & Referendum Participants, and our database of donations, loans, election/referendum spending & party accounts", with common searches such as "Q2 2026 Donations to Parties", "Regulated Donee Donations October 2026" and "Party spending in the 2026 Scottish Parliament Election". Its export links go to /api/csv/Donations and /api/pdf/Donations; a test request to the CSV endpoint returned HTTP 200 text/csv with a header row (ECRef, RegulatedEntityName, Value, AcceptedDate, DonorName, ...) and Q2 2026 rows. That endpoint is the site's export, not a documented public API, so access is recorded as web and bulk. Party donations are reported quarterly; spending returns follow each election.
Licence checked 2026-11-01: not verified. The search site footer shows "© 2026 The Electoral Commission" and links only to Accessibility, FAQs, Site map and Privacy notice on the main site, which sits behind a Cloudflare challenge; no copyright or reuse statement was found. See also uk-electoral-commission-election-data.
